Title: Why Is My Sourdough Flat? 5 Fixes for Beginners

Title: The Sourdough Poke Test: Underproofed, Ready or Overproofed?
Description: Flour a finger and press about half an inch into the dough. Springs right back: underproofed. Springs back slowly and leaves a small dent: ready to bake. Dent stays: overproofed, bake now anyway.
Keywords: sourdough poke test, is my sourdough proofed, overproofed sourdough

Title: Underproofed vs Overproofed Sourdough: Read Your Crumb
Description: Underproofed: tight dense crumb, a tunnel under the crust. Overproofed: flat wide loaf, even small holes, little oven spring. Just right: open, glossy, even holes top to bottom.
Keywords: sourdough crumb guide, underproofed vs overproofed sourdough, sourdough crumb

Title: Baker's Percentage Made Easy (Sourdough Cheat Sheet)
Description: Every ingredient is a percentage of the flour, and flour is always 100%. 500 g flour, 75% water = 375 g, 20% starter = 100 g, 2% salt = 10 g. The trap: your starter has flour and water too, so true hydration is 77.3%.
Keywords: bakers percentage, sourdough hydration calculator, bakers math

Title: Sourdough Starter Feeding Ratios Explained: 1:1:1 vs 1:5:5
Description: Starter : flour : water by weight. At 75F a healthy starter peaks in about 4-5 h at 1:1:1, 5-6 h at 1:2:2, 6-9 h at 1:3:3, about 10 h at 1:5:5 and 15-17 h at 1:10:10. Pick the ratio that peaks when you want to mix.
Keywords: sourdough starter feeding ratio, sourdough starter feeding schedule, starter ratio chart

Title: Bulk Fermentation Time by Temperature (Sourdough Chart)
Description: Why recipe times don't work in your kitchen: dough temperature. Roughly 8-12 h at 70F, 5-7 h at 75F, 4-6 h at 78F with 20% starter. Warmer dough needs less rise before shaping. Watch the dough, not the clock.
Keywords: bulk fermentation time chart, sourdough bulk fermentation temperature, sourdough timing

Title: Is My Sourdough Starter Ready? (Skip the Float Test)
Description: Your starter is ready when it at least doubles within 4-6 hours of a 1:1:1 feed, 2-3 days in a row, is domed and bubbly and smells pleasantly sour. The float test often fails for wet or whole-grain starters.
Keywords: is my sourdough starter ready, sourdough starter float test, sourdough starter tips

Title: Sourdough Starter: Normal or Not? Hooch, Smells and Mould
Description: Grey liquid (hooch), nail-polish smell, a dry crust and the day 4-6 slump are all normal: feed it. Pink or orange streaks or fuzzy mould are not: throw it out and start again.
Keywords: sourdough starter hooch, sourdough starter mold, sourdough starter smells like acetone

Title: Sourdough Schedule for People Who Work 9-5
Description: Feed your starter 1:5:5 before work, mix at 5:30 pm, folds in the evening, shape around 10 pm and cold proof overnight. Bake the next morning or after work. The fridge is your pause button.
Keywords: sourdough schedule working full time, sourdough baking schedule, overnight sourdough

Title: Weekend Sourdough Timeline: Start to Finish
Description: Friday night: feed the starter. Saturday: mix at 8 am, folds until 10:30, shape when bulk is done, then into the fridge. Sunday morning: bake from cold.
Keywords: weekend sourdough schedule, sourdough timeline, sourdough for beginners

Title: How to Make a Sourdough Starter: Day by Day
Description: Day 1: 50 g whole wheat or rye + 50 g water. Days 2-3: discard and feed. Days 4-6: the normal slump, don't restart. Days 7-10: feed twice a day. Ready when it doubles in 4-6 h, 2-3 days running.
